findings.title: Cloud Firestore documents can be deleted by unauthorized users
findings.remediation: Tighten Firestore rules so deletes require proper authorization.

findings.title: Cloud Firestore accepts unauthorized writes
findings.remediation: Tighten Firestore rules so writes require proper authorization.

findings.title: Realtime Database entries can be deleted by unauthorized users
findings.remediation: Set RTDB rules so `.write` (which governs delete) requires proper authorization.

findings.title: Realtime Database is readable by unauthorized users
findings.remediation: Set RTDB rules so `.read` requires proper authorization (never `".read": true` or a bare `auth != null`).

findings.title: Realtime Database accepts unauthorized writes
findings.remediation: Set RTDB rules so `.write` requires proper authorization.

findings.title: Storage objects can be deleted by unauthorized users
findings.remediation: Restrict deletes: `allow delete: if request.auth != null && <ownership/role check>;`.

findings.title: Storage bucket contents are listable
findings.remediation: Set Storage rules to require proper authorization, e.g. `allow read: if request.auth != null && <ownership/role check>;` — never `allow read: if true;` or a bare `request.auth != null`.

findings.title: Storage bucket accepts unauthorized uploads
findings.remediation: Restrict writes: `allow write: if request.auth != null && <ownership/role check>;`.

findings.title: Anonymous authentication enabled
findings.detail: Any unauthenticated attacker can mint a valid Firebase ID token, satisfying rules that only check request.auth != null.
findings.remediation: Disable Anonymous sign-in in Firebase Console > Authentication > Sign-in method (unless required, and then never treat request.auth != null as authorization).
